title: OmniGuard SOC Alert Contract & Graph Schema
description: The single alert contract every detection engine posts to POST /alerts, and the Neo4j property graph built from it. This file documents what backend/models.py and backend/graph.py actually implement - if they disagree, the code is right and this file is stale.

SeverityEnum.description: Analyst triage priority. Lowercase only - the dashboard uses these values as CSS class names.

SourceEnum.description: Which subsystem produced the alert. 'manual' is for analyst-submitted and test alerts.

StatusEnum.description: Triage state. Set by the dashboard, not by the engine.

AlertCreate.description: What a detection engine POSTs to /alerts. One contract for all engines - there is no per-engine payload. Fields not relevant to a given engine are simply omitted.

host.description: Hostname of the affected machine. Required. Becomes a Host node keyed on 'hostname'.

user.description: Account involved, if attributable. Network-only detections usually have none. Becomes a User node.

src_ip.description: Source IP of the affected host. Becomes an IP node and a Host-[:HAS_IP]->IP edge.

dst_ip.description: Destination IP, typically the C2 listener. Becomes an IP node.

domain.description: Domain involved. From TLS SNI for beacon alerts, from the visited URL for phishing alerts. Becomes a Domain node.

mitre_technique.description: MITRE ATT&CK technique ID. Becomes a Technique node so alerts can be grouped by technique across engines.

confidence.description: Detector confidence as a fraction, not a percentage. 0.87, never 87.

description.description: Human-readable summary shown to the analyst

dst_port.description: SpectraC2. Destination port. Stored as a property on the Alert-[:REPORTED_DST_IP]->IP edge.

beacon_interval.description: SpectraC2. Dominant beacon period in seconds from the FFT. Edge property.

mean_jitter.description: SpectraC2. Mean timing jitter in seconds. Edge property.

process_name.description: SpectraC2 / EDR. Originating binary. Becomes a Process node when combined with pid.

pid.description: SpectraC2 / EDR. OS process id. Combined with host it forms the Process key 'host:pid'.

target_url.description: VerifyEye. Full URL of the phishing page. Becomes a URL node, which links every host hit by the same lure.

action_endpoint.description: VerifyEye. Where the credential form would submit. An off-domain action is the phishing signal. URL node property.

brand_target.description: VerifyEye. Brand the page impersonates, from logo detection. URL node property.

Alert.description: What the API stores and returns: AlertCreate plus two fields the server generates. Clients cannot set these - they are not accepted on input, so an alert_id cannot be forged and a timestamp cannot be backdated.

alert_id.description: Server-generated UUID. Returned in the POST response so the producer can reference it.

timestamp.description: Server-generated UTC time of receipt, ISO 8601.

neo4j_graph_schema.description: Built by backend/graph.py ingest_alert(), one transaction per alert. Two layers: REPORTED_* edges hang off an Alert and are the audit trail of what that alert observed; every other edge is a standing fact about the network and survives the alert being deleted. The entity layer is self-sufficient - it shows what connects to what without any Alert nodes in the picture, which is why the dashboard canvas renders entities only by default.

Alert.created_with: MERGE on alert_id, ON CREATE SET the rest

Host.note: Keyed on hostname rather than a separate host_id. The alert contract carries one host field.

IP.note: Same property whether the address appeared as a source or a destination, so one IP is one node.

Technique.note: A node rather than a property, so alerts can be grouped by ATT&CK technique across engines.

URL.note: Links every host hit by the same lure page. Campaign breadth.

Process.note: process_id is host + ':' + pid, so the same pid on two machines is two nodes.

relationships.description: The host this alert was observed on. Every alert has one.
Destination this alert reported. Connection detail lives on this edge, not on the IP node.
Standing fact: this account uses this machine
Hierarchy: page to its parent domain

relationships.when: dst_ip and domain are both present
relationships.description: This address serves this domain. Asserted from co-occurrence in a single alert, not DNS-verified - behind a CDN it may not hold.

deferred_relationships.reason: Needs a parent and target process plus evidence of injection. The contract carries one process per alert and no parent_pid, so there is no data behind it yet. Requires EDR telemetry.

constraints: CREATE CONSTRAINT host_unique IF NOT EXISTS FOR (h:Host) REQUIRE h.hostname IS UNIQUE
CREATE CONSTRAINT user_unique IF NOT EXISTS FOR (u:User) REQUIRE u.username IS UNIQUE
CREATE CONSTRAINT domain_unique IF NOT EXISTS FOR (d:Domain) REQUIRE d.domain_name IS UNIQUE
CREATE CONSTRAINT ip_unique IF NOT EXISTS FOR (i:IP) REQUIRE i.address IS UNIQUE
CREATE CONSTRAINT alert_unique IF NOT EXISTS FOR (a:Alert) REQUIRE a.alert_id IS UNIQUE
CREATE CONSTRAINT technique_unique IF NOT EXISTS FOR (t:Technique) REQUIRE t.id IS UNIQUE
CREATE CONSTRAINT url_unique IF NOT EXISTS FOR (u:URL) REQUIRE u.url IS UNIQUE
CREATE CONSTRAINT process_unique IF NOT EXISTS FOR (p:Process) REQUIRE p.process_id IS UNIQUE
CREATE INDEX alert_timestamp_idx IF NOT EXISTS FOR (a:Alert) ON (a.timestamp)
CREATE INDEX alert_severity_idx IF NOT EXISTS FOR (a:Alert) ON (a.severity)

spectrac2.description: Encrypted C2 beacon, dominant interval ~60s with 18s jitter

verifyeye.description: Credential form impersonating Microsoft 365; form action posts off-domain

minimal.$comment: The four required fields. Everything else is optional - engines send what they have.

changes_from_v1: One AlertCreate replaces the separate VerifyEyeAlert and SpectraC2Alert definitions. Adding a third engine means no new model.
severity is lowercase only. It was accepted in both cases and uppercased, which broke the dashboard's CSS class names.
host replaces host_id; domain replaces sni.
alert_id and timestamp are generated by the server and are not accepted on input, so they cannot be forged or backdated.
confidence is a fraction (0.87), never a percentage (87).
Added a Technique node so alerts can be grouped by ATT&CK technique across engines.
Connection detail (port, beacon_interval, mean_jitter) sits on the REPORTED_DST_IP edge rather than a separate COMMUNICATED_WITH edge.

Alert edges renamed to the REPORTED_* family. The old names (TARGETS_HOST, FROM_SRC_IP, TO_DST_IP) read as if the alert were an actor - 'the alert came from this IP' - when an alert is an observation. Every edge now reads as a true sentence when you say it aloud.
